2027-06-14.title: Monday of the Eleventh Week in Ordinary Time
readings: See, now is the acceptable time … as having nothing, and yet possessing everything
The Lord has made known his salvation
But I say to you, Do not resist an evildoer
2027-06-14.alt: Weekday of Ordinary Time, Week 11 (Year I). Liturgical colour: green.
2027-06-14.verse: But I say to you, Do not resist an evildoer. But if anyone strikes you on the right cheek, turn the other also;
theo: St Paul writes to the Corinthians as a co-worker of God, and he speaks with urgency: “As we work together with him, we urge you also not to accept the grace of God in vain.” He quotes the prophet Isaiah, “At an acceptable time I have listened to you, and on a day of salvation I have helped you,” and then he adds his own commentary, like a man pointing at a clock: “See, now is the acceptable time; see, now is the day of salvation!” Grace is not something to be saved for later. Today is the day. Then Paul describes what his ministry has cost him, so that no one can say he preached for gain: “through great endurance, in afflictions, hardships, calamities, beatings, imprisonments, riots, labors, sleepless nights, hunger.” But the list does not end in complaint. It turns into a string of glorious paradoxes: “We are treated as impostors, and yet are true; as unknown, and yet are well known; as dying, and see, we are alive; as punished, and yet not killed; as sorrowful, yet always rejoicing; as poor, yet making many rich; as having nothing, and yet possessing everything.” This is the life of someone who belongs to the crucified and risen Christ. The world sees weakness and loss; God sees a man who possesses everything. The Psalm gives the reason for this joy: “O sing to the Lord a new song, for he has done marvelous things.”

In the Gospel we continue the Sermon on the Mount, and Jesus quotes one of the oldest laws of the ancient world: “You have heard that it was said, ‘An eye for an eye and a tooth for a tooth.’” We often think of this law as cruel, but in its time (Exodus 21:24) it was a limit on revenge: no more than an eye for an eye, not a life for an eye, not a whole family for one insult. Jesus now goes much further. “But I say to you, Do not resist an evildoer. But if anyone strikes you on the right cheek, turn the other also.” A blow on the right cheek, given by a right hand, is a backhanded slap: an insult more than an injury. Jesus says: do not answer insult with insult. If someone sues you for your coat, give your cloak as well; “if anyone forces you to go one mile, go also the second mile.” Roman soldiers could force a local man to carry their baggage for a mile, as Simon of Cyrene was forced to carry the cross. Jesus says: surprise him by going further than he demands. These are not rules for being weak. They are a way of breaking the chain of revenge with a stronger force, the force of goodness. The Church does not read this as a command to let the innocent be harmed: protecting the weak and legitimate defence remain duties of love (Catechism 2263–2265), and no one should remain in a home where they are being abused. But in the daily insults, quarrels and injustices of family, office and neighbourhood, the disciple of Jesus refuses to pay back evil for evil.
outline: Ask: when someone hurts me, what is my first reaction? To hit back, to sulk, or to bless?
Point 1 · Now is the acceptable time
Do not receive the grace of God in vain; today is the day of salvation.
Paul's sufferings become a song of paradox and joy.
Jesus breaks the chain of revenge with the stronger force of goodness.
“If anyone forces you to go one mile, go also the second mile.”
live: Do today the good thing you have been putting off: a confession, a reconciliation, a visit.
When someone asks you for a small service today, do a little more than they ask, with a smile.
2027-06-14.prayer: Lord God, now is the acceptable time and today is the day of salvation: do not let us receive your grace in vain. Give us the spirit of St Paul, who was sorrowful yet always rejoicing, poor yet making many rich, having nothing and yet possessing everything. Lord Jesus, you did not answer insult with insult, and on the cross you prayed for those who struck you. Teach us not to pay back evil for evil, to turn the other cheek to the small insults of each day, and to go the second mile in love. Amen.
altar: At the altar we receive the one who did not resist the evildoer: he offered his back to those who struck him and gave his life for those who took it. In the Eucharist this self-giving love is made present, the one sacrifice of the cross offered for us, and from it we receive the strength to go the second mile.

quick: Paul urges the Corinthians not to receive the grace of God in vain: now is the acceptable time, now is the day of salvation.
He describes his sufferings as a minister of Christ: sorrowful yet always rejoicing, poor yet making many rich, having nothing yet possessing everything.
Jesus replaces “an eye for an eye” with a new way: turn the other cheek, give your cloak as well, go the second mile.
2027-06-14.action: Answer one unkind word today with a kind one, or do more than you are asked for someone who demands your help.
2027-06-14.question: When I am wronged, do I keep the chain of revenge going, or do I break it with goodness?

family.explain: Long ago people said: if someone hurts you, you may hurt them back the same amount. Jesus says something new: do not hit back. If someone is unkind, be kind. If someone asks you to help, help even more than they ask. That is how we stop quarrels from growing. It is not easy, but Jesus helps us.
family.intention: We pray for children and teachers in the new school year, that classrooms may be places of kindness and not of bullying.
family.ask: Ask: “When someone in our family is unkind, how can we answer with kindness instead of anger?”

illus: In a busy office in Kochi, a senior clerk was known for shouting at the younger staff. One morning he threw a file on the desk of a new employee and blamed her loudly for a mistake that was not hers. She said nothing. At lunch she noticed that he had not eaten; she knew he was diabetic and had heard that his wife was in hospital. She quietly placed a packet of food and a cup of tea on his desk. He looked at her for a long moment and said nothing. The next day he came to her desk and apologised, the first time anyone in that office had heard him do so. She had gone the second mile. (An illustrative story.)

pm.open: Lord, you have done marvellous things. Make us witnesses of your love today, and break in us every chain of revenge. Amen.
share: See, now is the acceptable time; see, now is the day of salvation! (2 Corinthians 6:2). What grace of God am I putting off for later?
As having nothing, and yet possessing everything (2 Corinthians 6:10). What does it mean for me that Christ is my wealth?
If anyone forces you to go one mile, go also the second mile (Matthew 5:41). Who is asking me for more than I want to give?
pm.resp: The Lord has made known his salvation.
interc: For priests, religious and missionaries, that like Paul they may serve with endurance and joy.
For those who suffer insults and injustice, that they may be strengthened and protected.
For victims of violence in their own homes, that they may find safety and help.
For students and teachers at the start of the new school year.
For our group, that we may answer evil with good.
pm.close: Father, your Son taught us to turn the other cheek and to go the second mile. Give us his heart, so that we may overcome evil with good. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, St Paul says today: see, now is the acceptable time; see, now is the day of salvation! (2 Corinthians 6:2). We often say: later I will go to confession, later I will pray more, later I will make peace with my brother. Paul says: now. God's grace is offered today. Tomorrow is not promised to us.

Then Paul tells us what his life as an apostle was like: beatings, imprisonments, sleepless nights, hunger. And yet he says: we are sorrowful, yet always rejoicing; poor, yet making many rich; having nothing, and yet possessing everything (2 Corinthians 6:10). How is this possible? Because Paul has Christ, and the one who has Christ has everything. Many of our grandparents lived this way: they had little money, but they had faith, and they were rich.

In the Gospel Jesus asks something very difficult: do not resist an evildoer. But if anyone strikes you on the right cheek, turn the other also (Matthew 5:39). Jesus does not mean that we should allow the weak to be harmed, or that a wife should stay with a husband who beats her. The Church teaches that we must protect the innocent. But in the small insults of daily life, the harsh word, the unfair blame, the rude neighbour, Jesus asks us not to hit back.

And he asks even more: if anyone forces you to go one mile, go also the second mile (Matthew 5:41). Do more good than is demanded. This is how a family, an office, a parish is healed. Revenge makes the circle of evil bigger; goodness breaks it. Let us ask Jesus today for this grace, and let us use it now, for now is the day of salvation. Amen.
kids: Children, what do you do when your brother or sister hits you? Many of us want to hit back! Jesus says: do not hit back. Be kind instead. And if someone asks you to help, help even more than they ask. If Amma asks you to carry one bag, carry two! This is called going the second mile. It makes Jesus very happy, and it makes your home a happier place.

intro: Theme: “If anyone forces you to go one mile, go also the second mile.”
The day of salvation is today, the paradoxes of the apostle, and the goodness that breaks the chain of revenge.

sub: Do not receive grace in vain.
q: Thus says the Lord: In a time of favor I have answered you, on a day of salvation I have helped you;
See, now is the acceptable time; see, now is the day of salvation!
points.apply: Do this week the good thing you have been postponing: a confession, a reconciliation, a visit to the sick.

q: Though the fig tree does not blossom, and no fruit is on the vines; though the produce of the olive fails, and the fields yield no food; though the flock is cut off from the fold, and there is no herd in the stalls, yet I will rejoice in the Lord; I will exult in the God of my salvation.
as sorrowful, yet always rejoicing; as poor, yet making many rich; as having nothing, and yet possessing everything.
points.apply: Thank God this week for one loss or hardship through which he has made you richer in faith.

sub: An eye for an eye: a limit on revenge.
q: If your enemies are hungry, give them bread to eat; and if they are thirsty, give them water to drink;
Do not be overcome by evil, but overcome evil with good.
points.apply: Answer one insult or unfair demand this week with an unexpected act of kindness.

concl: Grace is offered today: the apostle who has Christ possesses everything, even in poverty and pain.
Jesus breaks the chain of revenge with a stronger force, the goodness that goes the second mile.
2027-06-14.resolve: Each day this week, do one thing more than you were asked, with love.
